webhooks_user.title: User Webhooks
webhooks_user.card_help: Send events about your own notes (reminder triggered, note created or shared) to external services such as ntfy or n8n via webhooks.
webhooks_user.description: Poznote sends an HTTP POST request with a JSON payload to each registered endpoint when one of your notes triggers a subscribed event: a reminder firing, a note being created or publicly shared. Only your own notes are concerned. If a secret is set, the payload is signed with HMAC-SHA256 in the X-Poznote-Signature-256 header.
webhooks_user.access_denied: Access denied. User webhooks are disabled on this instance.
webhooks_user.app_url_unset: No instance URL is configured, so the payloads carry no direct note link (data.note.url is null). Ask an administrator to set it on the admin Webhooks page.
webhooks_user.app_url_unset_admin: No instance URL is configured, so the payloads carry no direct note link (data.note.url is null). Set it on the admin Webhooks page.

event_help.user_created: A user account was created, by an admin, through the API or an SSO signup. Payload: the user profile and the creation source.
event_help.user_updated: A user profile changed: username, email, name or admin role. Payload: the updated profile and the list of changed fields.
event_help.user_activated: A previously deactivated user account was re-enabled. Payload: the user profile.
event_help.user_deactivated: A user account was deactivated and can no longer sign in. Payload: the user profile.
event_help.user_deleted: A user account was deleted. Payload: the profile as it was before deletion.
event_help.signup_cap_reached: An SSO signup was refused because the instance reached its maximum number of users. Payload: the cap and the attempted username and email.
event_help.quota_notes_reached: A user action was blocked because their notes quota is reached. Payload: the user, the limit and the current count.
event_help.quota_storage_reached: A user action was blocked because their storage quota is reached. Payload: the user, the limit and the current usage.
event_help.reminder_due: One of your note reminders reached its trigger time; other users' reminders never trigger your webhooks. Full payload: the note (id, title, workspace, direct link) and the reminder message.
event_help.reminder_due_title: Same trigger as reminder.due but without the reminder message: identifiers plus the note title and direct link.
event_help.reminder_due_minimal: Same trigger as reminder.due but identifiers only (note id, reminder id, trigger time): no note content leaves the instance. Details can be fetched through the REST API.
event_help.note_created: A note was created in your account, from the interface or the REST API. Payload: metadata only (note id, title, type, workspace, folder, direct link), never the note content.
event_help.note_shared: A public share link was published for one of your notes. Payload: the note (id, title, workspace, direct link), the public token and URL, and whether the link is password protected.

s3_settings.title: S3 Attachment Storage
s3_settings.description: Store note attachments in an S3-compatible object storage instead of the local disk.
s3_settings.description_benefit: Particularly useful if you have many or large attachments: the server disk stays light, and the complete backup zip can skip the S3 attachments; when everything stays on local disk, the export can become very heavy, slow, or even fail with a timeout.
s3_settings.description_scope: The setting applies to all users of this instance.
s3_settings.attachments_only_note: Only the attachment files are concerned.
s3_settings.enable_description: New attachments are written to the bucket. Files still on local disk keep working and can be migrated below.
s3_settings.endpoint_description: Base URL of the S3 API. Examples: https://s3.amazonaws.com, http://minio:9000, https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
s3_settings.region_description: Leave "us-east-1" for MinIO/Garage and providers that ignore the region.
s3_settings.path_style_description: Keep enabled for MinIO, Garage and most self-hosted servers. Disable only if your provider requires virtual-host style (bucket.endpoint).
s3_settings.test_success: Connection successful, the bucket is reachable.
s3_settings.migration_description: Move existing attachment files between the local disk and the bucket, for every user of the instance. Migration runs in batches and can be safely interrupted and resumed.
s3_settings.migrate_to_local: Bring files back to local disk
s3_settings.confirm_to_s3: Move all local attachment files (all users) to the bucket?
s3_settings.confirm_to_local: Download all bucket attachments back to the local disk (all users)?
s3_settings.footer_note: Attachments are stored under attachments/{user id}/ in the bucket and are always served through Poznote (the bucket can stay private).

s3_backup.title: S3 Backups
s3_backup.description: Upload complete backup archives (one ZIP per user, identical to the Complete Backup download) to an S3-compatible bucket, manually or automatically on a schedule.
s3_backup.description_scope: The setting applies to all users of this instance and is independent from the S3 attachment storage.
s3_backup.enable_description: Back up the selected users to the bucket on the schedule below. Manual backups from this page work as soon as the connection is configured, even with this switch off.
s3_backup.frequency_description: The first automatic backup runs within a few minutes of enabling, the next ones after the chosen interval.
s3_backup.retention_description: Older archives are deleted from the bucket after each backup. 0 keeps everything.
s3_backup.skip_s3_label: Skip attachments already stored in S3
s3_backup.skip_s3_description: When attachments live in an S3 bucket (S3 storage feature), leave them out of the archives instead of downloading them for every backup. Attachments on local disk are always included.
s3_backup.manual_description: Back up the selected users to the bucket right now, one user at a time.
s3_backup.manual_retention_warning: Every backup counts toward the retention limit, so a scheduled run can delete a manual archive just as a manual run can delete a scheduled one. To keep an archive for good, download it.

s3_backup.footer_note: Archives are stored under backups/{user id}/ in the bucket and can be restored with the standard "Restore / Import" page.
